newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso doing well but one term enough - poll.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso doing well but one term enough - poll.

text.p: Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso has performed well so far according to 43 percent of the electorate, his highest rating since he took office in 1995, but voters still would not like him take a second term, according to a poll published Sunday.

A survey by the local Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper of 5,000 people in 122 regions revealed that 46 percent opposed the idea of amending the constitution to permit the president to seek a second term. Another 16 percent approved the change, but only if it goes into force after Cardoso leaves office.
Only 31 percent backed changing the constitution to allow Cardoso to stand for office a second time, up from 25 percent in the previous survey in June, Folha said.
The number of people who think Cardoso has performed exceedingly well or well has also grown slightly compared with similar polls.
After nine months in office 42 percent ranked him highly in September 1995, and this number fell to 41 percent in December of the same year.
Cardoso has recently ended months of speculation by saying that he would like to stand for a second term of office.
